integrity: Every circular word through length six is exhaustively generated. Circular Parikh matrices are computed independently by scattered-subword averaging and by averaging products of letter Parikh matrices. Rule adjacency is independently reconstructed by constructive rewrites and pairwise decomposition testing.
scientific_limitations: The result is a finite minimal-boundary classification for full-support ternary circular words. It does not characterize ternary circular M-equivalence at arbitrary length and does not replace the published rules. Unindexed computational notes may contain the same census.
title: The first full-support failure of the circular Parikh rewriting rules occurs at length six
